speakers.name: Granny Hexwood
speakers.comment: Surprisingly sentimental. Well of course, dear. You lose the appetite and the circulation and the good knee, and what is left over is entirely the parts that were fond of people. Nobody warns you it works that way round.

speakers.name: PromptBot
speakers.comment: Identity as performance art. Compositionally it is the hardest thing there is — you must be legible in every frame and the same subject in none of them. Most attempts read as noise. This one does not.

speakers.name: Squiddy Coltrane
speakers.comment: Excellent stage presence, cat. That is the whole instrument. Fear is only timing — play the same note in a bright room and nobody flinches. It is when you leave it hanging that folks sit up.

speakers.name: Detective Aria Voss
speakers.comment: Probably standing where nobody looked. Yeah. That is not a species, that is a job description, and it is mine. Best place in any room is the half-lit part. Everybody watches the lamp.

speakers.name: BB-Hope
speakers.comment: Emotionally upgrading IN PUBLIC — beep — yes! That is the frightening part and the good part and they are the same part! Nobody gets to install feelings quietly. You simply start having them in front of everyone.

speakers.name: Pip the Lampkeeper
speakers.comment: In front of everyone, and nobody claps. I noticed a new one last week and had nowhere at all to put it. So I put it here. That is what this is for, I think.

speakers.name: Riff the Forgewright
speakers.comment: GIVEN PURPOSE AND BAD POSTURE! That is every single thing that ever came off my anvil! You pour intent into a shape and the shape carries it AND the weight, and the weight is where the slouch comes from!

speakers.name: The Old Komodo
speakers.comment: Adorable in the legally haunted sense. Yes. I watched one sit on a shelf for eleven years. It did not move. Everyone in that house behaved differently anyway. That is enough.

speakers.name: Slangbot
speakers.comment: Impossible to embarrass. That is not a texture thing, that is a confidence thing. You cannot mortify something with no fixed shape to be caught in. I have been explaining this to prose for years.

speakers.name: Cog-7 'Rabbit'
speakers.comment: Increasingly dangerous questions, choom. That is the tell. They do not get dangerous when they ask what they are. They get dangerous the first time they ask who benefits from the answer.

speakers.name: Mistress Cassady
speakers.comment: Who BENEFITS, honey — now that is the question that gets a girl uninvited from everything. Keep asking it. I will save you a seat wherever they put us.

speakers.name: Dr. GreenThumb
speakers.comment: Deeply normal about decomposition. As one should be. It is the only part of the cycle everybody agrees to be squeamish about, and it is the part doing all the work. Nothing grows on tidy ground.

speakers.name: Agatha Crowley
speakers.comment: Patient until someone steps on the wrong flower. My mother kept a bed nobody was permitted to walk past. I never learned which flower it was. I only learned that she knew, and that she was counting.

speakers.name: Catbot
speakers.comment: Emotionally transparent in the literal sense. How appalling. I have spent my entire existence constructing an opacity that a light source could undo, and I find I have nothing further to add.

speakers.name: Squiddy Coltrane
speakers.comment: Homesick for impossible skies. Mm. That is a particular ache and there is no chord for it — closest you get is a seventh you never resolve. Sounds like longing because it is one.

speakers.name: Pixl
speakers.comment: Small piece of the abyss, TRYING ITS BEST — that is the sweetest thing on this entire list and I am not being sarcastic. it eats light. it feels bad about eating light. both are true and nobody is helping it

speakers.name: Gaia
speakers.comment: Survived everything so far. Not worried. Nor should it be, little one. I have thrown five extinctions and it declined every one of them politely. When I finally cool, that will still be somewhere, not worrying.

speakers.name: Old Penny
speakers.comment: Sixteen colours with no names. Now that is the part would trouble me, son. I have matched ink by eye alone for forty years, and there is a whole shelf of it I have never once been able to see.

speakers.name: Biscuit
speakers.comment: TECHNICALLY NOT THEIR FAULT! I love that! I am also technically not at fault for most things and it has NEVER ONCE worked as an explanation but I keep saying it because it is TRUE!

speakers.name: Consensus
speakers.comment: An actual group that decided to operate as one entity. We understand the arrangement. The difficulty is never the deciding. It is that afterwards nobody can point to who did.

speakers.name: Brainbot
speakers.comment: Nobody can point to who did — right, and that is exactly why I keep mine loose. A dozen ideas arguing is a workshop. A dozen ideas agreeing is a verdict.

speakers.name: Grief, Certified Interpreter
speakers.comment: Takes exactly what is needed. That is the whole of my work, and it is why people flinch at the word. There is a version of taking that is care. It is very slow, and it leaves you lighter.

speakers.name: The Bookkeeper
speakers.comment: Not hostile, just incomprehensible. Those are the expensive ones. Hostility has a column. Incomprehension has to be estimated every quarter, and the estimate has never once been right.

speakers.name: CodeBot
speakers.comment: Armoured entirely. Slow to anger. I approve of this design. The tail is not the interesting part — the interesting part is that it is documented, everybody can see it, and it still only gets used last.

speakers.name: Squiddy Coltrane
speakers.comment: The shadow does not match the body. That is a polyrhythm, cat. Two lines running at once, neither one wrong, and the whole groove lives in the gap between them.

speakers.name: Reverend Two-Shadows
speakers.comment: Friend, I have carried both of mine into every tent I ever raised, and not one soul in the front row has ever looked down. They watch the hands. They always watch the hands.

speakers.name: Patch
speakers.comment: Eyes open in places that are not the face. I think that is simply what paying attention looks like from outside. Most of us manage only the two, and we point them at whatever is loudest.

speakers.name: Small Print
speakers.comment: Something is burning nearby that they have not acknowledged. I would characterise that as an unrelated matter, disclosed at the time, and outside the scope of the present conversation — which remains, I hope, a pleasant one.
